description: Parameter dictionary for seals emitted by BATEN IN, the on-device document analysis application. Declares the MEANING, value domain and AUTHORITY of each causal parameter — not how it is computed. Published per Causal Seal SPEC §3.3.

authority_values.observed: the emitter directly observed the value at generation time
authority_values.asserted: supplied to the emitter without independent verification
authority_values.derived: computed by the emitter from other state
authority_values.attested: produced/verified by a trusted control plane

engine.model.meaning: Identifier of the language model that wrote the report.

engine.reader.meaning: The causal reading engine that selected which passages of the sources governed the report.

engine.workspace.meaning: Where the text was executed: on the device itself, or by a named online provider.

identity.agents.meaning: Weights of the four orthogonal reading agents (FLVH bases), as set before the run. Format 'fv=N fh=N lv=N lh=N', summing to 100.

shaping.max_tokens.meaning: Output budget ceiling applied to the writing step.

shaping.sections.meaning: Number of sections the reading engine retained from the sources.

context.sources_count.meaning: Number of source documents sealed into the vault for this run.

context.sources_bytes.meaning: Total size in bytes of those sealed source documents.

notes: Parameter class names are fixed by SPEC §3.2 (identity / engine / field / shaping / context / x). BATEN IN previously emitted a 'sources.' class, which is NOT part of the standard and was rejected by the reference verifier; it is now carried under 'context.'.
engine.model is 'asserted': the emitter names the model it loaded, without an immutable revision digest. No stronger claim is made.
Seals emitted by the application carry no 'signature' member. Integrity (Level 1) is offline and free; authenticity (Level 2) is produced server-side, where the private key resides.
